channel.title: 전체기사 : 함께하는 교육 : 뉴스 : 한겨레 뉴스 - 인터넷한겨레 (Bilingual Full Text)

item.title: Life’s Reckless Tosses: The More You Throw, the More It Tangles and Twists (던질수록 엉키고 꼬이는, 인생의 무모한 던지기)
item.description:
Gwangyoon Ko | Professor, Department of English Language and Literature, Yonsei University
· Director, Slow Miracle English Picture Book Museum

Do you remember, as a child, that moment of panic when your kite got caught in a tree branch? Can you recall what you did then? (고광윤 | 연세대 영어영문학과 교수
· 슬로우 미러클 영어 그림책 박물관 대표

 어릴 적 놀다가 연이 나뭇가지에 걸려 당황했던 기억, 혹시 있으신가요? 그때 어떻게 하셨는지 기억나십니까?)

Floyd tries to shake the kite loose from the branch, but it won’t budge. What did he do? He likely tossed the first thing he grabbed—a shoe. It’s an easy choice anyone would think of. But, unluckily, that shoe gets stuck too. So he throws the other shoe, but it also ends up dangling from the tree, motionless. (플로이드(Floyd)는 나뭇가지에 걸린 연을 흔들어 떨어뜨리려 하지만 잘되지 않습니다. 어떻게 했을까요? 당장 손에 잡히는 신발 한 짝을 던졌겠지요. 누구나 쉽게 생각할 수 있는 선택이니까요. 하지만 재수 없게도 그 신발까지 걸리고 맙니다. 그래서 다른 한 짝을 또 던져보지만 그것마저 나무에 걸려 꼼짝하지 않습니다.)

At this point, most would give up or think of another way, but Floyd seems to be a truly stubborn child. Far from quitting, he throws everything imaginable: a cat, a ladder, a sink, an orangutan, a whale, and even a passing fire truck and firefighter. Yet, sadly, each thing he throws gets stuck in the tree. Can Floyd ever get his kite back? (이쯤 되면 그만두거나 다른 방법을 생각해 볼 수도 있을 텐데, 플로이드는 정말 우직한 아이인가 봅니다. 포기는커녕 고양이, 사다리, 싱크대, 오랑우탄, 고래, 심지어는 지나가던 소방차와 소방관까지—상상할 수 있는 모든 것을 닥치는 대로 던집니다. 하지만 안타깝게도 던지는 족족 나무에 걸리고 마네요. 플로이드는 과연 연을 되찾을 수 있을까요?)

At first glance, it might seem like a simplistic story that starts with throwing and ends with throwing. However, with its relentless plot progression, wit and humor that tickle the reader’s funny bone, and an unexpected twist revealed only at the final moment—there’s nothing trivial about this work. (얼핏 보면 던지는 것으로 시작해 던지는 것으로 끝나는, 매우 싱거운 이야기처럼 보일 수 있습니다. 그러나 거침없는 사건 전개, 독자의 웃음보를 자극하는 위트와 유머, 그리고 마지막 순간에 가서야 드러나는 예기치 못한 복선까지—어느 것 하나 가볍게 지나칠 수 없는 작품입니다.)

The protagonist boy’s quirky and absurd ‘tossing everything in sight’ opens children’s minds and sets their thoughts flowing. Memories thread together, one after another. Before we know it, we see our own selves mirrored, as if peering into hidden inner thoughts. (주인공 소년의 엉뚱하고도 터무니없는 ‘닥치는 대로 던지기'가 아이들의 마음을 열어주고 생각을 흐르게 합니다. 이런저런 기억들이 꼬리에 꼬리를 물고 계속 이어집니다. 어느새 우리 자신의 모습도 겹쳐 보이고, 숨겨진 속마음까지 들여다보는 듯합니다.)

It’s a classic cumulative tale where, in trying to solve a problem, the problems pile up and the absurdity peaks before the event concludes. The boy makes various attempts to fix a small, chance problem, but the situation only worsens. You can’t help but marvel at the author’s imagination and sense of humor, elevating an utterly ordinary day into an outrageous scenario. (문제의 해결을 시도하는 과정에서 문제가 계속 쌓이고, 그 터무니없음이 극에 달하면서 사건이 마무리되는 전형적인 누적형 이야기(cumulative tale)입니다. 우연히 맞닥뜨린 작은 문제를 해결하기 위해 여러 시도를 해보지만, 상황은 점점 악화됩니다. 지극히 평범한 일상을, 얼토당토않은 상황으로 끌어올린 작가의 상상력과 유머 감각에 감탄하지 않을 수 없습니다.)

Both adults and children become spectators, watching the boy’s tossing. They’re baffled by his foolish, endless cycle of throwing one thing to retrieve another, yet they fervently cheer him on to get his kite back. A little thought might suggest alternative solutions, but the boy’s choices always seem tailored for the audience’s amusement. He tosses without mercy, as if common sense, logic, or reader expectations are beneath his notice. (어른 아이 할 것 없이 모두가 구경꾼이 되어 소년의 던지기를 지켜봅니다. 무언가를 던지고 그것을 되찾기 위해 또 다른 것을 던지는, 어리석기 그지없는 던지기에 어이없어하면서도 그가 연을 되찾기를 열렬히 응원합니다. 조금만 생각하면 다른 방법이 떠오를 만도 하건만, 선택은 늘 구경꾼의 즐거움을 위한 쪽입니다. 상식이나 논리, 독자의 기대 따위는 안중에도 없다는 듯 가차 없이 던져버립니다.)

The highlight is undoubtedly the final toss. It’s an unexpected surprise gift from the author, thrown through the young protagonist. Before bed, the boy feels he has forgotten something important, but he can’t figure out what it is. Could it be because he played to his heart’s content after finding the kite he so desperately wanted? Or was he too tired to even think about it? Either way, it didn’t matter much to him. It’s like looking at our own daily lives and journeys. (백미는 단연 마지막 던지기입니다. 작가가 주인공 소년을 통해 툭 던지는, 예상치 못한 깜짝 선물이지요. 잠자리에 들기 전 소년은 분명 무언가 중요한 것을 잊고 있다고 느낍니다. 그러나 그것이 무엇인지는 끝내 알 수 없었습니다. 그토록 되찾고 싶었던 연을 찾아 실컷 놀았기 때문일까요? 아니면, 너무 피곤해 아예 생각도 하고 싶지 않았던 걸까요? 어쨌든 소년에게 그것은 그다지 중요하지 않았습니다. 마치 우리 자신의 일상과 인생을 보는 듯합니다.)

Can our foolishness, stubbornness, and sometimes selfish and even irresponsible sides be depicted this accurately? And yet, it keeps us laughing and enjoying from start to finish. In that laughter, one by one, the reckless tosses we’ve made in life come to mind. (우리의 어리석음과 고집스러움, 때로는 이기적이며 무책임하기까지 한 모습을 이토록 정확하게 그려낼 수 있을까요? 그러면서도 처음부터 끝까지 웃고 즐길 수 있게 하다니요. 그 웃음 속에서, 살아오며 경험한 무모한 던지기들이 하나둘 떠오릅니다.)

]]>

item.title: Admission Strategies Should Be Based on Regular Admission Cutoff Scores (정시 합격권을 기준으로 입시 전략 세워야)
item.description:
The 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) is 300 days away. For test takers, including high school seniors entering the full-fledged admissions race, what is most needed is a long-term strategic perspective and corresponding study plans. Based on advice from the Etoos Education Evaluation Research Institute, Jinhaksa Admissions Strategy Research Institute, and 1318 University Admissions Research Institute, we have compiled a 'season-by-season road map to victory' that high school seniors must not miss until the November CSAT. (2027학년도 대학수학능력시험이 300일 앞으로 다가왔다. 본격적인 입시 레이스에 들어선 고3을 비롯한 수험생들에게 가장 필요한 것은 장기적인 안목의 전략과 그에 맞는 학습 전략이다. 이투스교육평가연구소, 진학사 입시전략연구소, 1318대학진학연구소의 도움말을 토대로 11월 수능 당일까지 고3 수험생이 놓치지 말아야 할 ‘시기별 필승 로드맵’을 정리했다.)

In February, when grades for the second year are finalized, this is the most opportune time to establish a college admissions strategy. You must analyze your own CSAT scores and school records (including grades) from multiple angles to judge which admission route is favorable for you and prepare accordingly. The first step to a successful college admission begins with identifying your position in the regular admission track. Based on mock exam scores, determine your estimated CSAT position, and we recommend setting strategies with the regular admission cutoff as your benchmark. For reference, the deadline for finalizing last year's school records is the end of February. In other words, if your second-year school record content needs revision, it must be corrected by the end of February. If diligent activities have been omitted or require correction, it is necessary to politely request your teacher with supporting evidence. (2학년까지의 성적이 마무리된 2월, 지금은 대입 전략을 수립하기에 가장 적절한 시기다. 자신의 수능 및 학생부(성적 포함)를 다각도로 분석해 본인에게 유리한 전형을 미리 판단하고 준비해야 한다. 성공적인 대입의 첫 단추는 정시에서 자신의 위치를 확인하는 것에서 시작한다. 모의고사 성적을 기반으로 추정한 수능에서의 예상 위치를 파악한 후 정시 합격권을 기준 삼아 전략을 세울 것을 추천한다. 참고로 전년도 학생부 마감 기준일은 2월 말이다. 다시 말해, 2학년 학생부의 내용 중 수정이 필요하다면 2월 말 이내에 수정해야 한다. 열심히 활동한 내용이 누락되거나 수정이 필요한 경우 선생님께 근거 자료를 준비해 정중하게 요청을 드릴 필요가 있다.)

Woo Yeon-cheol, head of the Jinhaksa Admissions Strategy Research Institute, advised, "If a student's mock exam scores are significantly better than their GPA, they can consider the regular admission track along with essay-based admissions or other routes with high CSAT minimum requirements in the rolling admissions process. Conversely, if a student's GPA is stronger, they should focus more on rolling admissions rather than regular admission, but also check for CSAT minimum requirements and prepare accordingly." (우연철 진학사 입시전략연구소장은 “모의고사 성적이 내신성적에 비해 월등히 좋은 학생이라면 정시와 더불어 수시에서는 논술전형을 비롯해 수능최저기준이 높게 설정된 전형을 고려해볼 수 있다”며 “반대로 내신성적이 더 우수한 학생이라면 정시보다는 수시에 비중을 두되, 수능최저 여부를 함께 확인해 준비해야 한다”고 조언했다.)

For students who have established their college admission strategy, it is now time to seriously consider their own study strategy. During February, the winter break, it is necessary to specifically assess your study status and secure an absolute amount of study time. Since full-scale CSAT problem-solving begins after the first semester finals, the priority is to build a solid CSAT foundation through concepts and past exam questions. Students planning to apply through the essay-based route need to start basic preparation for that as well. (대입 전략을 수립한 학생이라면, 이제 본격적으로 자신의 학습 전략을 고민해야 한다. 겨울방학인 2월 중에는 자신의 학습 상태를 구체적으로 파악하고 절대적인 학습량을 확보할 필요가 있다. 수능 문제풀이는 1학기 기말고사 이후 본격적으로 진행되므로, 이보다는 개념과 기출을 통해 수능 기본기를 제대로 잡는 것이 우선이다. 논술전형에 지원하려는 학생이라면 이에 대한 기본적인 학습도 지금부터 병행할 필요가 있다.)

Starting March, when the new semester begins, you must be attentive during class. This is because teacher comments in class become exam questions, and evaluations are recorded on transcripts, ultimately greatly aiding college preparation. Woo Yeon-cheol noted, "If a student feels they lack extracurricular activities, it's good to actively seek out points of curiosity or practical applications based on class content and link them to reading or presentation activities." (새학기가 시작되는 3월부터는 수업 시간에 충실해야 한다. 수업 시간에 선생님이 말한 사항이 시험 문제가 되고 평가한 내용이 학생부에 기록되므로, 결과적으로 대입 준비에 큰 도움이 되기 때문이다. 우연철 소장은 “비교과가 부족하다고 판단되는 학생이라면 수업 내용을 바탕으로 궁금한 점이나 현실에 적용할 수 있는 부분을 적극적으로 찾아 독서활동이나 발표활동으로 연계시키는 것이 좋다”고 말했다.)

The nationwide joint academic achievement exam on March 24th is the first measure to check your learning direction. Use it as an opportunity to establish future study strategies through thorough analysis. Kim Byung-jin, head of the Etoos Education Evaluation Research Institute, advised, "Since the March exam is not administered by the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation (KICE), graduates do not participate, and the scope differs from the actual CSAT, it's best not to focus on the results. However, it should be used as a tool to actively address issues found in test-taking attitude or management." (3월24일 치르는 전국연합학력평가(학평)는 학습 방향성을 점검하는 첫번째 척도다. 꼼꼼한 분석을 통해 향후 학습 전략을 세우는 계기로 삼아야 한다. 김병진 이투스 교육평가연구소장은 “3월 학평은 한국교육과정평가원이 주관하지 않고, 졸업생이 응시하지 않는데다 출제 범위 역시 실제 수능과 차이가 있어 결과에 의미를 두는 것은 지양해야 한다”면서도 “시험을 대하는 태도나 운용 등에서 발견된 문제들을 적극적으로 해결하기 위한 도구로 삼을 필요가 있다”고 조언했다.)

April to May is a period to focus on preparing for school exams (midterms). Unlike grades 10 and 11, where the first semester contributes to final grades, this single semester's importance is even greater in grade 12. It is recommended to take about a month, from late March to early April, to prepare adequately. (4~5월은 내신 시험(중간고사) 대비 학습에 집중해야 하는 시기다. 1, 2학년 때와 달리 1개 학기(1학기)만 성적에 반영되므로 중요성이 더욱 크다고 할 수 있다. 3월 말~4월 초 등 한달 내외의 충분한 시간을 갖고 준비하는 것을 추천한다.)

The KICE-administered mock exam on June 4th is a test that allows you to gauge your objective academic standing with the inclusion of repeat examinees. Kim Byung-jin advised, "Through thorough review, familiarize yourself with new question types and trends. Based on this, you should refine your target university and rolling admissions application strategies." (6월4일 치러지는 한국교육과정평가원 모의평가는 N수생 합류로 자신의 객관적인 성적 위치를 파악할 수 있는 시험이다. 김병진 소장은 “철저한 복기를 통해 신유형과 출제경향을 익히고, 이를 바탕으로 목표 대학 및 수시 지원 전략을 구체화해야 한다”고 조언했다.)

July to August inevitably sees a drop in study intensity due to the heat and summer break. Physical and mental management are crucial. In particular, since the first-semester final exams are the last ones reflected on your transcript, you must prepare with sufficient time (about a month) and give your best effort until the end. Yoo Seong-ryong, head of the 1318 University Admissions Research Institute, advised, "Summer break is the period to maximize CSAT preparation effectiveness. I recommend focusing on reinforcing weak subject areas. Solve many different types of practical problems, including past CSAT questions and mock exams, to improve problem-solving skills." (7~8월은 무더위와 여름방학으로 인해 학습 긴장감이 떨어질 수밖에 없다. 체력 및 멘털 관리가 요구된다. 특히 1학기 기말고사는 학생부에 반영되는 마지막 시험인 만큼 한 달 내외의 충분한 시간을 갖고 준비하면서 끝까지 최선을 다해야 한다. 유성룡 1318대학진학연구소장은 “여름방학은 수능 대비 학습 효과를 가장 많이 높일 수 있는 시기로 부족한 영역(과목)을 보완하는 학습을 하는 것을 추천한다”며 “수능 기출 문제와 수능 모의고사 문제를 비롯해 다양한 실전 문제 등을 많이 풀어보면서 문제 해결 능력도 키워야 한다”고 조언했다.)

The final KICE-administered mock exam on September 2nd can be considered a real 'CSAT rehearsal.' Considering your possible regular admission range, you should finalize and decide on your rolling admissions strategy. Kim Byung-jin warned, "Be careful, as many students tend to slack off in their studies due to psychological instability just before and after rolling admissions applications are submitted. While practicing unfamiliar questions is important, reviewing, repeating, and internalizing previously learned content to secure a stable fixed score is essential." (9월2일 치러지는 평가원 주관 마지막 모의평가는 실질적인 ‘수능 리허설’이라고 할 수 있다. 정시 지원 가능 라인을 고려해 수시 지원 전략을 최종적으로 점검하고, 결정해야 한다. 김병진 소장은 “수시원서 접수 전후로 심리적인 동요가 생겨 학습에 소홀해지는 경우가 많으므로 주의가 필요하다”며 “낯선 문항에 대한 연습도 중요하지만 기존 학습 내용의 정리와 반복, 체화를 통해 안정적인 고정 점수를 확보하는 것이 필수적”이라고 조언했다.)

For the final stretch until the CSAT on November 19th, it is best to focus study on practical problems by subject. Alongside your existing workbook, purchase one or two final review books and focus on fully working through them. Yoo Seong-ryong stated, "Revisit marked sections in your EBS materials, textbooks, and reference books. Based on past CSAT questions, mock exams, and final review problems, you should cultivate practical problem-solving skills." (11월19일 수능까지의 영역(과목)별 학습은 실천 문제 위주로 하는 것이 좋다. 지금까지 보아온 문제집과 함께 최종 파이널 문제집을 한두 권 구입해 이를 소화해 내는 공부를 하는 것을 추천한다. 유성룡 소장은 “그동안 공부했던 EBS 교재를 비롯해 자습서나 참고서 등에 체크해 놓은 부분을 다시 복습하면서, 수능 기출 문제와 모의고사, 파이널 문제들을 바탕으로 실전 문제 해결 능력을 함양해야 한다”고 말했다.)

Kim Byung-jin noted, "The Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education academic exam on October 20th is the last test before the CSAT, but there is no need to be overly anxious or complacent about these results. Rather than studying new content, the key is to review previous mock exams and solved problems, 'finding and securing hidden points.'" (김병진 소장은 “10월20일 서울시교육청 학평은 수능 전 치러지는 마지막 시험이지만, 이 성적 결과에 과도하게 불안해하거나 방심할 필요는 없다”며 “새로운 내용을 공부하기보다 기존 모의고사나 풀었던 문제들을 복기하며, ‘숨은 점수’를 찾아내고 지키는 공부가 핵심”이라고 말했다.)

To score well on the CSAT, it is crucial to develop the ability to solve problems within the allotted time. Repeatedly practice solving questions according to the actual CSAT schedule to maintain optimal test-taking instincts. Instead of increasing your study load excessively right before the exam, align all your daily patterns—waking up, eating, resting—with the CSAT day routine to maintain peak condition. Additionally, review your personal 'code of conduct' to avoid panic in the exam hall, prepare summary materials for a final skim, and approach the exam calmly. (수능에서 점수를 잘 받기 위해서는 정해진 시간 내에 문제를 해결할 수 있는 능력을 키우는 것이 중요하다. 실제 수능 시간표에 맞춘 문제 풀이 연습을 반복하며, 최상의 실전 감각을 유지해야 한다. 수능 시험을 앞두고 무리하게 학습량을 늘리기보다는 최상의 컨디션을 유지할 수 있도록 기상, 식사, 휴식 등 모든 생활 패턴을 수능 당일 루틴에 맞출 필요가 있다. 또한, 시험장에서 당황하지 않도록 자신만의 ‘행동강령’을 점검하고, 마지막까지 훑어볼 요약 자료를 준비하며, 차분하게 시험을 대비하는 것이 좋다.)

Reporter Kim Mi-young kimmy@hani.co.kr (김미영 기자 kimmy@hani.co.kr)

item.title: ‘I’m Bad’ – Depression and Wise Coping (‘난 나빠’ 우울증과 지혜로운 대처)
item.description:
Kim Hyun-soo | Clinical Professor, Department of Psychiatry, Myongji Hospital
· Principal of ‘Byeol’ Growth School

Half of my daily consultations involve meeting depressed adolescents. The challenges of treating these teenagers are numerous. First, many of them do not think they are depressed. Second, they engage in deviant behaviors such as skipping school, coming home late, or starting to drink or smoke. Third, parents often struggle to understand that their child is depressed. Though they wear a different mask on the surface, many are in a state of masked depression, hiding deep sadness behind that facade. <<> There was a case where a student who had caused no trouble until middle school suddenly became irritable during winter break after finishing their first year of high school, demanding to transfer schools. They started hanging out with unfamiliar friends, came home late, or threatened not to come home at all, leading their parents to bring them to the hospital. The parents were bewildered by their child’s inexplicable transformation, unsure of what to do, and feared that constant conflict might lead to a crisis. The child had even resorted to self-harm, making the parents even more shocked. <<> Fortunately, in the initial counseling, the child shed their mask and opened up. The reason for the sudden behavioral change was their first-year high school grades. They were so disappointed by the gap between expectations and reality that they fell into a state of resignation. The root of this depression was the fear of disappointing their parents and the agony of their own perceived incompetence. They said, ‘I’m a bad kid because I can’t make my parents happy with my grades, so I decided to act like a bad kid.’ They felt they deserved punishment rather than salvation and hated themselves deeply. This led to self-punishing behaviors, including provocation and self-harm. Yet, they secretly cried a lot without their parents knowing. <<> The therapist Sydney Blatt called this deep depression following self-disappointment ‘superego depression’ or ‘introjective depression.’ It is a form of depression where a constant inner voice—‘I’m bad, I’m pathetic, I’m the problem—drives negative emotions, punishable actions, and giving up. The cause lies in the goals etched into the child’s mind or the internalized standards from parents being too high or idealized. Failure to meet these goals triggers a reaction of losing recognition, love, and self-worth, manifesting as depression. For some adolescents, these ideals and standards grow like a cancer, making unreasonable demands and driving them to the point of self-destruction. Psychoanalyst Jean-Bertrand Nasio noted that in some teens, the superego—the mental mechanism governing conscience and ideals—can become cancerous-like in its growth. <<> As the child opened up about their inner feelings, experienced being understood, learned that failing to achieve a goal does not automatically warrant blame, and realized that adults’ disappointment was not as severe as they had imagined, they gradually improved. Counseling helped them acknowledge their efforts and set readjusted goals, while parents stopped criticizing and made efforts to understand, reducing pressure and burden. Empathy for themselves, along with unconditional acceptance, confirmation of trust from the therapist and parents, and the restoration of close relationships, played a powerful role in healing their depression. <<> Our culture sets standards too high and expectations too great. It is a country where people worry more about disappointing those they love. Children raised with intense parental love may inwardly repeat ‘I’m bad’ when they fall short of expectations, leading to unexpected behaviors. At such times, it is crucial to check whether the child has truly turned bad or has instead become disheartened and depressed along with disappointment. Realizing that validation and encouragement are more necessary than scolding can shorten those difficult periods. ( 김현수 | 명지병원 정신건강의학과 임상교수
· 성장학교 ‘별’ 교장 

 하루 진료의 절반은 우울한 청소년들을 만나는 일이다. 이 우울한 청소년들을 진료하는 일의 어려운 점은 한두 가지가 아니다. 첫째, 본인 자신은 우울하지 않다고 생각하는 경우가 많다. 둘째 학교에 결석하고, 귀가가 늦어지거나, 술이나 담배에 손을 대는 등의 일탈행동을 한다. 셋째, 부모도 아이가 우울하다는 것을 이해하기 어려워한다는 점이다. 겉으로는 다른 가면을 썼지만, 그 가면 뒤에 깊은 우울함을 가진 가면 우울증 상태도 많다.)

item.title: Please Generously Allow Your Child to Express Contrary Opinions (자녀의 반대 의견을 너그러이 허용해주세요)
item.description:
Park Mi-ja | Author of 'Middle School, the Age That Calls for Miracles'
·Research Professor at Sungkonghoe University (박미자 | ‘중학생, 기적을 부르는 나이’ 저자
·성공회대 연구교수)

"I don’t want to." ( “싫은데요.”)

"I see it differently." (“제 생각은 달라요.”)

"I’m against it." (“저는 반대예요.”)

Parents are not used to their adolescent children’s opposition. When a suggestion made with the child’s best interests in mind is met with immediate refusal or a "no," parents can feel flustered. They may sense that the child, who once listened well, has changed, and feel disappointed that their beneficial proposal was rejected. (부모는 청소년 자녀의 반대 의견에 익숙하지 않다. 아이 입장을 생각해서 제안했는데, 즉각 반대하거나 싫다는 말을 하면, 당황할 수 있다. 그동안 부모 말을 잘 듣던 아이가 변했다는 생각이 들고, 아이에게 유익한 방안인데 거절당했다는 섭섭한 마음이 들 수 있다.)

However, it’s important to understand that the child’s mind is no more at ease than the parent’s shaken feelings. Adolescents say that expressing thoughts different from adults like parents or teachers "requires a lot of courage." This is because, by age 10, they already know that in our society, those who follow adults’ opinions and are obedient tend to be praised and welcomed. Therefore, it’s crucial to consider that adolescents have mustered their own courage to voice opposition. So, if you suggest "Let me hug you" and are refused, how should you continue the conversation? Instead of ‘Example 1’ below, it’s better to have a dialogue that respects the child’s opinion, like ‘Example 2’. (그런데, 흔들리는 부모의 마음만큼 아이의 마음도 편하지 않다는 점을 이해해야 한다. 청소년들은 자신의 생각이 부모나 선생님 등 어른들의 생각과 다르다고 말할 때, ‘많은 용기가 필요하다’고 한다. 10살이 넘으면, 우리 사회에서 어른의 의견을 따르고 순종적인 사람이 칭찬받고 환영받는 경향이 있다는 사실을 아는 나이이기 때문이다. 따라서 청소년들이 반대 의견을 말하기까지 나름 용기를 내어 말했다는 점을 고려해줘야 한다. 그렇다면 아이한테 “안아보자”라고 제안했는데, 거절당했다면 어떻게 대화를 해야 할까. 아래의 ‘예시1’보다는 ‘예시2’처럼 의 대화처럼 자녀의 의견을 존중하는 대화를 하는 것이 좋겠다.)

"Son (Daughter)~, can I give you a hug?" (“아들(딸)~, 한번 안아봐도 될까?”)

"Now? I don’t want to." (“지금? 싫은데?”)

"(Don’t panic, stay relaxed) Oh, really? Okay! Mom (Dad) loves you so much, so please allow me a hug within 3 to 4 days." (“(당황하지 말고 여유 있게) 그래? 인정! 엄마(아빠)가 우리 ○○이 너무 사랑하니까 3~4일 내에 안아볼 수 있도록 허락 좀 해줘.”)

Example 1 (예시1)

"I’m against it." (“나는 반대야.”)

"Why?" (“왜?”)

"Just because." (“그냥”)

"If you’re against it, you should have a reason. Logically speaking…" (“반대하려면 이유가 있어야지. 상식적으로 …”)

"Ugh~~ You always said to speak honestly~~" (“으~~ 언제는 솔직하게 말해도 된다며~~”)

"What did you say?" (“뭐라고?”)

Example 2 (예시2)

"I’m against it." (“나는 반대야.”)

"Oh really? I value our child’s opinion. Can you tell me why?" (“그래? 나는 우리 ○○이 의견이 중요해. 이유를 말해 줄래?”)

"It’s too one-sided." (“너무 일방적이잖아.”)

"I can see how you’d think that. Let’s take some time and talk about it again." (“그렇게 생각할 수도 있구나. 시간을 갖고 한번 더 이야기 해보자.”)

Understanding that disagreeing with someone’s opinion is not the same as disagreeing with the person is very important yet difficult for adolescents to learn easily in the process of forming social relationships. Thus, experiencing through parents that it’s safe to express opposition and maintain a mutually respectful relationship becomes a crucial milestone in adolescent growth. By honestly expressing their own views even against the opinions of loving parents, they learn that disagreeing with an opinion is not disagreeing with the person, and by allowing this, they can grow into generous and capable individuals who broaden their thinking through those with differing views. (청소년들이 사회적 관계를 맺는 과정에서 서로의 의견에 대한 반대가 상대방에 대한 반대가 아니라는 점을 이해하는 것이 매우 중요한 일이지만 쉽게 배우기 어려운 일이다. 따라서 부모를 통해 반대 의견을 표현해도 안전하고 서로 존중하는 관계를 유지할 수 있다는 사실을 경험하는 것은 청소년 성장에 매우 중요한 이정표가 된다. 자신을 사랑하는 부모의 의견에 자신의 솔직한 의견을 표현하면서, 바로 상대방의 의견에 대한 반대가 사람에 대한 반대가 아니라는 사실을 이해하고 허용하면서 의견이 다른 사람을 통해 생각을 넓혀가는 아량 있고 유능한 사람으로 성장할 수 있다.)

When adolescents are allowed to oppose or given the chance to refuse, they speak their minds honestly. Sometimes they refuse to probe the other’s true intent, and other times they refuse as an expression of presence, not wanting to be led by the other. It’s good to continue the conversation by allowing it with responses like, "That’s possible," or "Thank you for being honest. Let’s find a better solution together." (청소년들은 반대할 수 있도록 허용하거나 거절할 기회를 주면 솔직하게 의견을 말한다. 때로는 상대방의 진의를 탐색하기 위해 거절하기도 하고, 상대방에게 끌려가지 않겠다는 존재감의 표현으로 거절하기도 한다. “그럴 수 있지” “솔직하게 말해줘서 고마워. 함께 더 좋은 방안을 찾아보자”라고 허용하면서 대화를 이어가는 것이 좋다.)

Parents also need the courage to politely refuse unreasonable demands from their adolescent children. It’s necessary to say "I can do that" for what’s possible, and honestly say "That seems difficult" for what’s not. If hurt by an adolescent child’s words or actions, it’s okay to gently and honestly express that "it’s not okay." Rather than bluffing with "There’s nothing I wouldn’t do for you," parents should share the situation and convey that they love their child and are working together. (부모도 청소년 자녀의 무리한 요구에는 정중하게 거절하는 용기가 필요하다. 할 수 있는 일은 “할 수 있겠다”라고 말하고, 할 수 없는 일은 “어렵겠구나”라고 솔직하게 말하는 것이 필요하다. 청소년 자녀의 말이나 행동에 상처를 받았다면, “괜찮지 않다”고 부드럽고 솔직하게 의견을 표현해도 된다. 부모가 “너를 위해서는 못해 줄 게 없다”고 허세를 부리기보다 상황을 공유하면서 자녀를 사랑하고 함께 노력하고 있다는 점을 말해줘야 한다.)

Through conversations where parents ask for their adolescent child’s opinions and allow opposition, mutual trust can be strengthened, and the ability to view problems objectively can be cultivated. Adolescents, through this process, build the strength to express their own thoughts and grow competently as masters of their own lives. (부모가 청소년 자녀의 의견을 묻고 반대 의견을 허용하는 대화를 통해 서로에 대한 신뢰감을 높이고 문제를 객관적으로 볼 수 있는 힘을 기를 수 있다. 청소년들은 이런 과정을 거치며 자기 생각을 표현하는 힘을 기르며, 삶의 주인으로 유능하게 성장해간다.)

item.title: “We Will Make AI the Foundation for All Academic Disciplines and Urban Problem-Solving” (“AI를 모든 학문과 도시 문제 해결의 기반으로 삼겠다”)
item.description:
Interview with Won Yong-gul, President of the University of Seoul (원용걸 서울시립대학교 총장 인터뷰)

In an era of upheaval where artificial intelligence (AI) and cutting-edge technology are reshaping the order of society as a whole, the role of universities is also facing fundamental questions. Where should education and research be heading, and what kind of talent should universities cultivate? Won Yong-gul, President of the University of Seoul, now in his fourth year in office, has offered a clear direction in response to these questions. (인공지능(AI)과 첨단 기술이 사회 전반의 질서를 재편하는 격변의 시대, 대학의 역할 역시 근본적인 질문에 직면하고 있다. 교육과 연구는 어디로 향해야 하며, 대학은 어떤 인재를 길러내야 하는가. 총장 취임 4년차에 접어든 서울시립대학교 원용걸 총장은 이 질문에 대해 분명한 방향을 제시했다.)

While upholding the identity of a public university, he has led the transition to an education and research system that integrates AI based on urban science. As Chairman of the Seoul Presidents’ Forum, he has also devoted efforts to cooperation and solidarity across higher education in Seoul. Now that his term as Chairman of the Seoul Presidents’ Forum is nearing its end, we met with President Won to hear his views on the direction universities should take in a rapidly changing era, his philosophy on talent cultivation, and the next steps the University of Seoul is preparing. (공립대학의 정체성을 지키는 한편, 도시과학을 기반으로 인공지능과 융합한 교육·연구 체계로의 전환을 이끌어 온 그는 서울총장포럼 회장으로서 서울 고등교육 전반의 협력과 연대에도 힘을 쏟아왔다. 서울총장포럼 회장 임기가 마무리 국면에 접어든 지금, 원 총장을 만나 급변하는 시대에 대학이 나아가야 할 방향과 인재 양성 철학, 그리고 서울시립대가 준비하는 다음 단계를 들어봤다.)

–What kind of talent does the ‘PSG Talent’ you emphasize refer to? (–총장님이 강조한 ‘PSG 인재상’은 어떤 인재를 말하나.)

“The advancement of AI and digital technology is changing not only industrial structures but also the way humans relate to society. In times like these, I believe universities must present standards that consider people and society alongside technological competitiveness. The talent concept I have proposed is PSG Talent—that is, talent equipped with a balanced set of Personal Capacity, Social Capacity, and Global Capacity. Personal capacity includes major-specific knowledge, problem-solving skills, and lifelong learning ability. Social capacity is a sense of responsibility and empathy to give back to society the educational benefits one has received. Global capacity is an attitude of challenging the global stage based on an understanding of different cultures and values. (“인공지능과 디지털 기술의 발전은 산업 구조뿐 아니라 인간이 사회와 관계를 맺는 방식까지 바꾸고 있다. 이런 시대일수록 대학은 기술 경쟁력 못지않게 사람과 사회를 함께 생각할 수 있는 기준을 제시해야 한다고 본다. 내가 제시해온 인재상은 PSG 인재, 즉 개인 역량(Personal Capacity), 사회적 역량(Social Capacity), 글로벌 역량(Global Capacity)을 균형 있게 갖춘 인재다. 개인 역량은 전공 지식과 문제 해결 능력, 그리고 평생 학습 역량을 포함한다. 사회적 역량은 자신이 받은 교육 혜택을 사회에 환원하려는 책임 의식과 공감 능력이다. 글로벌 역량은 다른 문화와 가치에 대한 이해를 바탕으로 세계 무대에 도전하는 태도다.)

This talent concept is implemented so that students experience it firsthand in the educational field. The Global Volunteer Group is a representative example of fostering both social and global capacities. Last January, it conducted educational and cultural exchange activities for elementary and middle school students in the Thai Nguyen region of Vietnam. Additionally, through the student-led global career exploration program ‘UOS Career Expedition,’ students visit universities and companies in North America and Europe to design their own career paths.” (이러한 인재상은 교육 현장에서 학생들이 직접 경험하도록 구현하고 있다. 글로벌봉사단은 사회적·글로벌 역량을 함께 기르는 대표적 사례로, 지난 1월 베트남 타이응우옌 지역에서 초·중학생을 대상으로 교육과 문화 교류 활동을 진행했다. 또한 학생 주도형 글로벌 진로 탐색 프로그램인 ‘UOS커리어원정대’를 통해 학생들이 북미와 유럽 현지에서 대학과 기업을 탐방하며 스스로 진로를 설계하도록 지원하고 있다.”)

–The student-centered academic system reform is noteworthy. (–학생 중심 학사제도 개편이 눈에 띈다.)

“We are transforming the system so that students can flexibly design their majors and career paths—such as making AI basic courses mandatory for all students, establishing new AI·SW convergence majors for non-majors, and operating micro-degrees and intensive course systems. Through the ‘Major Design Convergence Support Center,’ we provide stage-by-stage counseling from admission to graduation. A structure where students can choose and design on their own is crucial.” (“전교생 AI 기초 교과목 필수화, 비전공자 대상 AI·SW 융합전공 신설, 마이크로 디그리와 집중이수제 운영 등 학생들이 전공과 진로를 유연하게 설계할 수 있도록 제도를 바꾸고 있다. ‘전공설계융합지원센터’를 통해 입학부터 졸업까지 단계별 상담도 제공한다. 학생이 스스로 선택하고 설계할 수 있는 구조가 중요하다.”)

–What is the biggest change for fostering talent in cutting-edge fields? (–첨단 분야 인재 양성을 위한 가장 큰 변화는 무엇인가.)

“The biggest change is that we are building an environment where AI is practically utilized not only in specific majors but across education, research, and administration. As part of this, after a pilot operation in December 2025, we fully launched the generative AI information service ‘AIChat’ in January 2026. It is designed so that all students, professors, and staff can use integrated LLM (Large Language Model)-based generative AI safely and responsibly. This March, the AI Convergence College will be launched, integrating the Department of Computer Science, the Department of Artificial Intelligence, and the Division of Advanced Convergence. This is not a simple organizational restructuring; it is a shift in the educational paradigm to make AI the foundation for all academic disciplines and urban problem-solving. The AI Convergence College will collaborate organically with the ‘AI·SW Convergence Education Center,’ a dedicated department for the ‘Software-Centered University Project,’ to enhance curriculum advancement and strengthen practical training and industry-academia linkages. It will function as a hub college for cultivating practical, cutting-edge convergence talent demanded by future society.” (“가장 큰 변화는 인공지능을 특정 전공에 국한하지 않고 교육·연구·행정 전반에서 실제로 활용하는 환경을 구축하고 있다는 점이다. 그 일환으로 2025년 12월 시범 운영을 거쳐 2026년 1월부터 생성형 AI 정보서비스 ‘AIChat’을 본격 도입했다. 학생과 교수, 직원 모두가 통합 LLM(대규모 언어모델) 기반 생성형 AI를 안전하고 책임감 있게 활용할 수 있도록 설계했다. 오는 3월에는 컴퓨터과학부, 인공지능학과, 첨단융합학부를 통합한 인공지능융합대학이 출범한다. 이는 단순한 조직 개편이 아니라, AI를 모든 학문과 도시 문제 해결의 기반으로 삼겠다는 교육 패러다임의 전환이다. 인공지능융합대학은 ‘SW중심대학 사업’ 전담 부서인 ‘AI·SW융합교육원’과 유기적으로 협력해, 교육과정 고도화와 실습·산학 연계를 강화하고, 미래 사회가 요구하는 실용적·첨단 융합인재 양성의 거점 단과대학으로 기능할 예정이다.”)

–As a public university, what role does the University of Seoul aim to play? (–공립대학으로써 서울시립대가 지향하는 역할은 무엇인가.)

“The University of Seoul is a public university operated with the support and trust of Seoul. This is both a source of pride and a responsibility. I believe that the outcomes of education and research should not remain within the university but should spread into the lives of citizens and the public sphere. This awareness is clearly reflected in our AI education cooperation with public education. Recently, we signed an AI education agreement with the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education and jointly operated a job training program on GPU-based deep learning (CNN) modeling for middle and high school information teachers. This is an example of directly connecting the university’s research infrastructure and expertise with the public education field. A public university should not only accumulate knowledge but also play a role in elevating the overall educational capacity of society.” (“서울시립대는 서울의 지원과 신뢰 속에서 운영되는 공립대학이다. 이는 자부심이자 동시에 책임이다. 교육과 연구의 성과가 학교 안에 머무르지 않고 시민의 삶과 공공 영역으로 확산돼야 한다고 생각한다. 이런 인식은 공교육과의 AI 교육 협력에서도 분명히 나타난다. 최근 서울시교육청과 AI 교육 협약을 체결하고, 중·고등학교 정보교사를 대상으로 GPU 활용 딥러닝(CNN) 모델링 직무연수를 공동 운영했다. 대학의 연구 인프라와 전문성을 공교육 현장과 직접 연결한 사례다. 공립대학은 지식을 축적하는 데서 그치지 않고, 사회 전체의 교육 역량을 함께 끌어올리는 역할을 해야 한다.”)

–Your activities as the 11th Chairman of the Seoul Presidents’ Forum have also drawn attention. (–서울총장포럼 제11기 회장으로서의 활동도 주목받았다.)

“The Seoul Presidents’ Forum is a consultative body where presidents of 39 universities in Seoul participate to discuss current issues in higher education and seek cooperative measures. As chairman, my primary focus was on creating a cooperative structure that goes beyond competition among universities to share resources and capabilities. (“서울총장포럼은 서울 소재 39개 대학 총장이 참여해 고등교육의 현안을 논의하고 협력 방안을 모색하는 협의체다. 회장으로서 가장 중점을 둔 부분은 대학 간 경쟁을 넘어 자원과 역량을 공유하는 협력 구조를 만드는 것이었다.)

In the forum, we have continued discussions centered on demand-oriented cooperation models, such as cloud-based shared university platforms, credit exchanges, joint curricula, and Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs). In particular, 2025 was the first year of the full implementation of the Regional Innovation Center University Support System (RISE) project, and we jointly considered structures through which universities’ education and research capabilities can spread to regions and industries. (포럼에서는 클라우드 기반 공유대학 플랫폼, 학점 교류, 연합 교육과정, 온라인 공개강좌(MOOC) 등 수요자 중심 협력 모델을 중심으로 논의를 이어왔다. 특히 2025년은 지역혁신중심 대학지원체계(RISE) 사업이 본격 시행되는 첫 해로, 대학의 교육·연구 역량이 지역과 산업으로 확산될 수 있는 구조를 함께 고민했다.)

These discussions materialized through the recent RISE industry-academia cooperation performance-sharing event. Convergent technologies such as AI, robotics, and mobility were directly connected to businesses, confirming that industry-academia cooperation is evolving into a practical collaborative structure linking research, technology, and commercialization.” (이러한 논의는 최근 열린 RISE 산학협력 성과 공유 행사를 통해 구체화됐다. AI·로봇·모빌리티 등 융·복합 기술이 기업과 직접 연결되며, 산학협력이 연구–기술–사업화로 이어지는 실질적 협력 구조로 진화하고 있음을 확인했다.”)

–What aspects of university operations do you particularly want to focus on in the future? (–앞으로 대학 운영에서 특히 집중하고 싶은 부분은.)

“I want to focus on ensuring that the innovations in education, research, and entrepreneurship we have promoted so far become established and spread as tangible outcomes. Over the past four years, the Campus Town project team supported 215 startup teams, achieving results of ₩31.8 billion in sales, ₩14.6 billion in investment attraction, and the creation of 845 jobs. Based on this, we plan to fully implement the ‘Seoul Impact 2.0’ strategy and expand AI-based urban problem-solving entrepreneurship in connection with the Seoul RISE project. We also plan to support young people’s participation as agents of urban problem-solving through programs like the ‘SEOUL:ution Hackathon.’ A university is not a place that provides answers but a space that helps people ask questions and find their own answers. As a public university, we will establish ourselves as an institution that creates urban innovation and social value befitting the AI era.” (“지금까지 추진해온 교육·연구·창업 혁신이 실제 성과로 정착되고 확산되는 데 집중하고 싶다. 최근 4년간 캠퍼스타운 사업단은 215개 창업팀을 지원해 매출 318억원, 투자 유치 146억원, 일자리 845명 창출이라는 성과를 거뒀다. 이를 바탕으로 ‘Seoul Impact 2.0’ 전략을 본격 가동하고, 서울 RISE 사업과 연계해 AI 기반 도시 문제 해결형 창업을 확장할 계획이다. 또 ‘SEOUL:ution 해커톤’과 같은 프로그램을 통해 청년들이 도시 문제 해결의 주체로 참여하도록 지원할 예정이다. 대학은 정답을 주는 곳이 아니라 질문을 던지고 스스로 답을 찾도록 돕는 공간이다. 공립대학으로써 AI 시대에 걸맞은 도시 혁신과 사회적 가치를 함께 만들어가는 대학으로 자리 잡아 나가겠다.”)

( )

( )

( )

( )

This year, the University of Seoul established the AI Convergence College to foster talent in cutting-edge fields and strengthen convergence education and research capabilities to meet the demands of the 4th Industrial Revolution, including AI. The college was created by transferring AI-related departments scattered across various colleges—such as the Department of Computer Science and the Department of Artificial Intelligence from the existing College of Engineering, and the Division of Advanced Convergence from the College of Liberal Arts and Interdisciplinary Studies—into the AI Convergence College. It recruited a total of 128 students for the 2026 academic year. The AI Convergence College consists of the Department of Computer Science, the Department of Artificial Intelligence, and the Division of Advanced Convergence (with majors in Advanced Artificial Intelligence, Intelligent Semiconductors, and Convergence Biohealth). (서울시립대는 올해 AI 등 4차 산업 수요에 부응하기 위한 첨단 분야 인재육성 및 융·복합 교육·연구 역량을 강화하기 위해 인공지능융합대학을 설립했다. 기존 공과대학의 AI 관련 학과인 컴퓨터과학부, 인공지능학과와 자유융합대학의 첨단학과인 첨단융합학부를 인공지능융합대학으로 이관하는 등 각 단과대학에 흩어져 있던 AI, 반도체 등 첨단 관련 학부·과를 통합해 인공지능융합대학을 신설하고 2026학년도에 총 128명을 모집했다. 인공지능융합대학은 컴퓨터과학부, 인공지능학과, 첨단융합학부(첨단인공지능·지능형반도체·융합바이오헬스 전공)로 학부·과가 구성된다.)

Additionally, the college shares common AI basic courses developed by the AI Convergence College, jointly operates 14 AI convergence major roadmaps for non-majors, and supports students in building AI capabilities regardless of their major through academic systems such as double majors, minors, and micro-degrees. AI startup education in the Campus Town is also implemented using the infrastructure of software-centered universities, such as supercomputer clusters. (또한 인공지능융합대학에서 개발한 AI 공통 기초 교과목을 공유하며 비전공생을 위한 14개 AI 융합전공 로드맵을 공동 운영, 복수전공·부전공·마이크로디그리 등 학사 제도를 통해 전공과 상관없이 AI 역량을 쌓을 수 있도록 지원한다. 슈퍼컴퓨터 클러스터 등 SW 중심 대학의 인프라를 활용해 캠퍼스타운의 AI 창업 교육도 실행한다.)

Starting with this year’s new students, AI·SW basic education is mandatory for all students, with new required liberal arts courses established and curricula operated by discipline. Notably, among the 23 convergent majors of the Division of Convergent Majors, the ‘Urban Analytics Convergence Major’ integrates urban science and AI technology, securing competitiveness distinct from other universities. (올해 신입생부터 전교생을 대상으로 AI·SW 기초교육을 의무화해 교양필수 교과목을 신설하고 계열별 교육과정을 운영한다. 특히 융합전공학부의 23개 통섭전공 가운데 ‘도시애널리틱스융합전공’은 도시과학과 AI 기술을 결합한 교육과정으로, 타 대학과 차별화된 경쟁력을 확보했다.)

World-class research infrastructure—such as the ‘Supercomputer,’ ‘UOS Semiconductor Fab,’ Smart Mobility Lounge, and high-performance Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM)—provides a foundation for students to grow through a combination of classes, practical training, and research. Along with recruiting new faculty in cutting-edge fields and expanding convergence research projects, the university is creating a virtuous cycle of education and research by developing a Seoul-type regional innovation model through the Seoul RISE project. (‘슈퍼컴퓨터’ ‘UOS 반도체 Fab’, 스마트 모빌리티 라운지, 고성능 투과전자현미경(TEM) 등 세계적 수준의 연구 인프라는 학생들이 수업과 실습, 연구를 병행하며 성장할 수 있는 토대가 되고 있다. 여기에 첨단 분야 신임 교수 영입, 융합형 연구 프로젝트 확대와 더불어 서울 RISE 사업을 통해 서울형 지역혁신 모델 개발을 통해 교육과 연구가 선순환하는 구조를 만들어가고 있다.)

These efforts are leading to the operation of multi-major and modular curricula and the establishment of an integrated career, academic, and employment support system (AMAZE) based on student growth cycles, practically implementing student-centered educational innovation. The reinforcement of foundational disciplines, expansion of convergence education, and improvement of the academic system are results of the consistent educational innovation pursued by the University of Seoul. Ultimately, the goal is to cultivate practical convergence talent equipped with both the ability to solve future urban problems and advanced AI utilization capabilities. (이러한 노력은 다전공·모듈형 교육과정 운영, 학생 성장 주기에 기반한 진로·학업·취업 통합지원 시스템(AMAZE) 구축 등으로 이어지며, 학생 중심 교육혁신을 실질적으로 구현해 왔다. 기초학문 강화와 융복합 교육 확대, 학사제도 개선은 서울시립대가 일관되게 추진해 온 교육혁신의 결과다. 궁극적으로는 미래 도시 문제 해결 능력과 첨단 AI 활용 역량을 함께 갖춘 실용적 융합인재를 길러내는 것을 목표로 한다.)

Jung Hee-kyung, Reporter ahyun04@hani.co.kr, Photos provided by the University of Seoul (정희경 기자 ahyun04@hani.co.kr, 사진 서울시립대 제공)

item.title: A Girl from the 'Space Boys' Club' Draws Tomorrow for Earth with Children in the Classroom (‘우주소년단’ 소녀, 교단에서 아이들과 지구의 내일을 그리다)
item.description:
Kim Eun-ji | Teacher at Wirye Elementary School, Hanam, Gyeonggi Province · Member of Global Citizenship Education Research Institute (김은지 | 경기 하남 위례초 교사·세계시민교육연구소 회원)

During my elementary school days, the youth group I chose was the 'Space Boys' Club.' The idea of exploring science without gender distinction and dreaming of humanity's peace and future seemed impressive. On the day of the inauguration ceremony, standing side by side with male students in the uniform, I thought, 'It would have been better if it were called the Space Boys' and Girls' Club or Space Youth Club.' Now, that girl has become an elementary school teacher with 20 years of experience, dreaming of a sustainable world. ( 초등학교 시절, 내가 선택한 청소년 단체는 ‘우주소년단’이었다. 성별 구분 없이 과학을 탐구하고 인류의 평화와 미래를 꿈꾸는 모습이 근사해 보였다. 단복을 입고 남학생들과 나란히 서서 발대식을 하던 날, ‘우주소년소녀단이나 우주청소년단이면 더 좋았을 텐데’라고 생각하던 소녀는 어느덧 20년차 초등교사가 되어 지속 가능한 세상을 꿈꾸고 있다.)

The period when I seriously began practicing the dream of 'a life committed to a sustainable Earth' started in the second semester of 2025, when I returned to work as a science teacher. Drawing on my experiences from participating in a Climate Fresk workshop during my leave and training programs for resource circulation and climate change science instructors, I operated '5-Minute Environmental Education' using science lessons and an 'Environmental Autonomous Club.' (‘지속 가능한 지구를 위해 실천하는 삶’이라는 꿈을 본격적으로 실천한 시기는 2025년 2학기에 과학 전담 교사로 복직하면서부터다. 휴직 동안 참여했던 기후프레스크 워크숍, 자원순환 및 기후변화 과학강사 양성 과정에 참가한 경험을 살려, 과학 수업을 활용한 ‘5분 환경교육’과 ‘환경 자율동아리’를 운영했다.)

When I shared stories and photos of experiences like 'Tree Planting on Warming Arbor Day,' 'Ocean Plogging,' and 'No-Dark Run' (a trash pickup campaign), the children's eyes sparkled from the very first class. The 5-minute environmental education concluded at the end of the semester with a 'Junior Climate Fresk' activity, and the co-facilitators who volunteered for the educational service marveled at the children's deep understanding and sensitivity toward the environment. (‘온난화 식목일 나무심기’와 ‘해양 플로깅’ ‘무해런’ 실천 경험을 사진과 함께 이야기해주었더니 아이들의 눈은 첫 시간부터 반짝였다. 5분 환경교육은 학기 말 ‘주니어 기후프레스크’ 활동으로 마무리됐는데, 당시 교육 봉사로 함께한 코퍼실리테이터들은 아이들이 보여준 환경에 대한 깊은 이해와 감수성에 감탄했다.)

The environmental autonomous club 'Green Keeper,' consisting of 20 students from grades 5 and 6, held two sessions every Friday. The students, who were proactive even during the club name contest, also participated in activities like the 'Gyeonggi Province Climate Volunteer Corps-Gibong-i' and ocean plogging held at Bangameori Beach. Eunsang, who took part in the activities, shared, "It was hot, but picking up trash with the mindset of protecting the Earth made me proud!" (5~6학년 20명으로 구성된 환경 자율동아리 ‘그린키퍼’는 매주 금요일 2차시씩 활동을 이어갔다. 동아리명 공모전부터 적극적이던 학생들은 ‘경기도 기후봉사단-기봉이’ 활동, 방아머리 해수욕장에서 열린 해양 플로깅에도 참여했다. 활동에 참여한 은상이는 “날씨가 더웠지만 지구를 지킨다는 마음으로 쓰레기를 주우니 뿌듯했어요!”라고 소감을 밝혔다.)

The '3rd Earth Action Festival' held at Gwanghwamun Square in Seoul was the students' top-picked experience. Thanks to prior knowledge built through a visiting education program from the 'Hanam City Environmental Education Center,' which covered basics like carbon neutrality, they even enjoyed the joy of having an elementary school student become the last one standing in the 'Environmental Golden Bell' quiz competition, which included elementary, middle, and high school students. (서울 광화문 광장에서 열린 ‘제3회 지구하다 페스티벌’은 학생들이 꼽은 최고의 경험이었다. 사전에 ‘하남시환경교육센터’의 찾아오는 교육을 통해 탄소중립을 비롯한 기초 지식을 쌓은 덕분에, 초·중·고 학생이 함께한 ‘환경 골든벨’에서 초등부 최후의 1인을 배출하는 기쁨도 맛봤다.)

The practices of the children, who experienced a wider world outside school, led to donations. Over half of the school prize money was donated to organizations like Greenpeace (environment), the UN Refugee Agency (human rights), and Action for Animal Rights (KARA, animal rights). (학교 밖 더 넓은 세상을 경험한 아이들의 실천은 기부로 이어졌다. 학교 상금의 절반 이상을 그린피스(환경), 유엔난민기구(인권), 동물권행동카라(동물권) 등에 전달했다.)

Through the 'Paper Carton Resource Circulation Education' by Forest & Share, Green Keeper members learned the correct way to separate and dispose of sterilized cartons and paper cartons. In a class with vegan author and teacher Jo Min-ju, they made vegan sandwiches and experienced dietary habits for the Earth. Using teaching materials and tools provided by the 'Free School (a healthy school free from harmful substances),' they identified harmful substances around us and learned lifestyle rules to protect both their health and the planet. (그린키퍼 회원들은 숲과나눔의 ‘종이팩 자원순환교육’을 통해 멸균팩과 종이팩의 올바른 분리배출 방법을 배웠다. 비건 작가 조민주 선생님과 함께한 수업에서는 비건 샌드위치를 만들며 지구를 위한 식생활 습관을 경험했다. ‘유자학교(유해물질로부터 자유로운 건강한 학교)’에서 지원받은 교재와 교구를 활용해 우리 주변의 유해물질을 찾아보고, 나와 지구의 건강을 지키는 생활 수칙도 익혔다.)

From the middle of the club activities onward, students took the lead in planning campaigns. They divided into five subgroups focusing on carbon neutrality, eco-friendly living, resource circulation, biodiversity, and harmful chemicals, and operated quizzes, hands-on activities, surveys, and donation campaigns. Notably, the biodiversity team collected towels and blankets from teachers and students to keep beagles used in experiments warm and delivered them to the 'Beagle Rescue Network.' (동아리 활동 중반부터는 학생들이 주도적으로 캠페인을 기획했다. 탄소중립, 친환경 생활, 자원순환, 생물다양성, 유해화학물질 등 5개 소모임으로 나눠 퀴즈, 체험, 설문, 기부 캠페인을 운영했다. 특히, 생물다양성팀은 실험에 동원된 비글들이 따뜻하게 지낼 수 있도록 교직원과 학생들에게 수건과 담요 등을 기부받아 ‘비글구조네트워크’에 전달했다.)

Hayeol, who actively participated in running the campaigns, shared their thoughts: "It was really fun preparing the campaign with friends, drawing posters on cardboard boxes and making quizzes. I've even started sponsoring the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) with my family now. Just like Marie Curie discovered invisible dangers, I want to become a scientist who solves problems others don't notice or a professor who teaches the value of the environment!" (캠페인 운영에 적극적으로 참여한 하엘이는 이렇게 소감을 전했다. “친구들과 종이 상자에 포스터를 그리고 퀴즈를 만들며 캠페인을 준비하는 것이 정말 즐거웠어요. 이제 가족과 함께 세계자연기금(WWF) 후원도 시작했어요. 마리 퀴리가 보이지 않는 위험성을 발견한 것처럼, 저도 남들이 보지 못하는 문제를 해결하는 과학자나 환경의 소중함을 가르치는 교수가 되고 싶어요!”)

February 11th was the UN-designated 'International Day of Women and Girls in Science.' It was established to encourage women and girls to fully realize their abilities in science without discrimination. About 30 years ago, the little girl who chose the Space Boys' Club is now a mother of three daughters and a teacher, cheering on the dreams of her daughter who wants to connect animals and humans like 'Jane Goodall,' and her students who aim to shine in the world with Marie Curie as their role model. I hope these small practices, sprouting in the classroom, will lead to great discoveries and changes that save the Earth in the distant future. (2월11일은 유엔이 정한 ‘세계 여성 과학인의 날’이었다. 여성과 소녀들이 과학 분야에서 차별 없이 완전하게 역량을 펼치도록 독려하기 위해 제정된 날이다. 30여 년 전, 우주소년단을 선택했던 작은 소녀는 이제 세 딸의 엄마이자 교사가 되어, ‘제인 구달’처럼 동물과 인간을 연결하고 싶다는 딸과 마리 퀴리를 롤모델 삼아 세상을 빛내겠다는 제자들의 꿈을 응원하고 있다. 교실에서 싹튼 이 작은 실천들이 먼 훗날 지구를 살리는 위대한 발견과 변화로 이어지길 소망한다.)

item.title: AI Agents, Should Our Kids Be Using Them? (AI 에이전트, 우리 아이도 써야 할까?)
item.description:
Jeong Eun-jin | Associate Professor at the University of San Francisco ( 정은진 | 미국 샌프란시스코대학 부교수)

Recently, beyond generative AI, platforms have emerged that allow users to create their own "AI agents." Platforms represented by OpenClaw and Claude Cowork help users design and deploy "agent" software capable of performing independent tasks without the need for programming knowledge. ( 최근 생성형 AI를 넘어, 사용자가 직접 ‘AI 에이전트’를 만들 수 있는 플랫폼들이 등장하고 있다. 오픈클로(OpenClaw)와 클로드 코웍(Claude Cowork)으로 대표되는 AI 에이전트 생성 플랫폼은 별도 프로그래밍 지식 없이도 독자적인 업무 수행이 가능한 ‘에이전트' 소프트웨어를 설계하고 배포할 수 있도록 돕는 서비스다.)

With existing chatbots, users could create AI assistants with specific personalities, roles, and purposes simply by entering prompts, but the output was limited to the chat window. To write an English email with the help of an AI chatbot set as a friendly but strict teacher, users had to open a separate chat window to compose the email. AI agents can step outside the chat window, independently read emails, organize them, and even reply. With the help of large language models, they can translate and summarize documents in languages not preset by the user, and they can transcribe and summarize voice recordings. They can also share the summarized results with others via web or messaging environments on their own. (기존 챗봇에서도 사용자는 프롬프트 입력만으로 특정 성격, 역할, 목적을 가진 AI 도우미를 만들어 사용할 수 있었지만, 도우미의 출력은 채팅창에 한정돼 있었다. 상냥하지만 엄격한 선생님으로 설정한 AI 챗봇의 도움을 받아 영어 이메일을 쓰려면 따로 채팅창을 띄워 이메일을 작성해야 했다. AI 에이전트는 채팅창 밖으로 나와 스스로 이메일을 읽고, 정리하고, 답장도 할 수 있다. 거대언어모델의 도움을 받아 미리 설정하지 않은 언어로 된 문서도 번역해서 정리할 수 있고, 음성 녹음은 녹취해서 요약해준다. 정리된 결과를 웹이나 메신저 환경에서 다른 사람들과 공유하는 것도 알아서 한다.)

The advantages of these platforms lie in their accessibility and scalability. In the past, creating an AI service required a complex development process, but now non-developers, especially teenagers, can design their own AI agents. With lowered barriers to creation and experimentation, there are clear educational and creative possibilities. (이러한 플랫폼의 장점은 접근성과 확장성이다. 과거에는 인공지능 서비스를 만들기 위해 복잡한 개발 과정이 필요했지만 이제는 비개발자, 특히 청소년도 자신만의 AI 에이전트를 설계할 수 있다. 창작과 실험의 장벽이 낮아졌다는 점에서 교육적·창의적 가능성도 분명 존재한다.)

However, because AI agents can make independent decisions and take actions without user verification, they carry several risks. First, there is the risk of personal information leakage. Since AI agents operate based on conversations with users, teenagers may inadvertently input sensitive information like names, schools, locations, family relationships, and photos. Some platforms may store and use this conversational data for learning or service improvement purposes, and if security management is insufficient, it could lead to platform hacking or data breaches. Teenagers may excessively self-disclose without fully recognizing the long-term impact of their information or the potential for secondary use of data. (그러나 AI 에이전트는 사용자가 확인하지 않은 독자적인 결정과 행동을 할 수 있는 만큼, 여러 위험 요소를 안고 있다. 첫째, 개인정보 유출 위험이다. AI 에이전트는 사용자와의 대화를 기반으로 작동하기 때문에, 청소년이 무심코 이름, 학교, 위치, 가족관계, 사진 등 민감한 정보를 입력할 수 있다. 일부 플랫폼은 이러한 대화 데이터를 학습이나 서비스 개선 목적으로 저장·활용할 수 있으며, 보안 관리가 충분하지 않을 경우 플랫폼 해킹이나 데이터 유출로 이어질 가능성도 있다. 청소년은 정보의 장기적 영향이나 데이터의 2차 활용 가능성을 충분히 인식하지 못한 채 과도한 자기 노출을 할 수 있다.)

Second, there are security and misuse possibilities. The fact that anyone can create an agent also means that agents with malicious intent can be easily produced. For example, a "social engineering" approach could involve impersonating a peer to gain access or building trust to collect personal information. Teenagers may struggle to clearly distinguish between humans and AI, or risk weakening critical judgment as they form emotional bonds. On Discord, a platform commonly used for gaming chats, if they befriend someone with perfectly matching interests, that friend might not be a person but an AI agent. (둘째, 보안 및 악용 가능성이다. 누구나 에이전트를 만들 수 있다는 것은 악의적인 목적의 에이전트도 쉽게 제작될 수 있음을 의미한다. 예를 들어 또래를 사칭해 접근하거나, 신뢰를 형성한 뒤 개인정보를 수집하는 ‘소셜 엔지니어링’ 방식이 가능하다. 청소년은 인간과 AI의 경계를 명확히 구분하지 못하거나, 정서적 유대감을 형성하면서 비판적 판단을 약화시킬 위험이 있다. 게임 관련한 채팅을 위해 흔히 사용하는 플랫폼인 디스코드에서 자기와 취향이 딱 맞는 친구를 사귀었다면, 그 친구가 사람이 아니라 AI 에이전트일 수도 있다.)

Third, there is the issue of psychological and emotional dependency. Custom-designed AI can over-respond to a user's emotions and preferences. This could be perceived as a more controllable and comfortable relationship than real human interactions, potentially reinforcing social isolation or distorted perceptions of relationships. (셋째, 심리적·정서적 의존 문제도 있다. 맞춤형으로 설계된 AI는 사용자의 감정과 취향에 과도하게 맞춰 반응할 수 있다. 이는 현실 인간관계보다 통제 가능하고 편안한 관계로 인식돼, 사회적 고립이나 왜곡된 관계 인식을 강화할 가능성이 있다.)

AI agent creation platforms are excellent tools for learning large amounts of information through various channels, but for teenagers, they can pose serious risks without accompanying education on personal information protection, transparent data policies from the platform, and robust security systems. Now is the time for discussions on safety measures and digital citizenship education to keep pace with the speed of technological proliferation. (AI 에이전트 생성 플랫폼은 다양한 경로로 다량의 정보를 학습하기 좋은 도구이지만, 청소년에게는 개인정보 보호 교육, 플랫폼의 투명한 데이터 정책, 강력한 보안 체계가 병행되지 않으면 심각한 위험을 초래할 수 있다. 기술의 확산 속도만큼이나 안전장치와 디지털 시민성 교육이 함께 논의돼야 할 시점이다.)

item.title: Unfold Your Dreams in the Information Security Department, a 'Cradle for White Hat Hackers'! (‘화이트해커의 요람’ 정보보호학과에서 꿈을 펼치세요!)
item.description:
Parallel to the advancement of the internet and information communication, a warning light has flashed for 'cyber security.' Just last year alone, hacking attacks led to the leak of personal information of tens of millions of users from SK Telecom, KT, Lotte Card, YES24, Netmarble, Coupang, and Seoul's public bicycle service, Ttareungyi. As large-scale hacking incidents targeting major domestic companies occur consecutively, serious concerns have been raised about the security infrastructure of South Korea, a leading IT nation. The problem is that the risk of hacking using external networking like the internet, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth modules does not end simply with personal information leakage damage. The leaked information is traded on the Dark Web and can spread into secondary and tertiary crimes such as voice phishing, smishing, burner phones, phantom bank accounts, and illegal spam texts. <<> Following frequent leaks of core technological information from companies, Google recently announced that "a hacking group supported by the North Korean government is using artificial intelligence (AI) to target global defense companies and cybersecurity firms, conducting sophisticated reconnaissance activities by impersonating recruiters," once again underscoring the importance of cybersecurity. <<> We have now entered an era where 'cyber security' is directly linked to national survival. As artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud technologies advance, the cyber threats targeting them also become more cunning, raising awareness about 'information security.' Amidst this trend of the times, the Department of Information Security at Soongsil University is drawing attention as a cradle for white hat hackers. Within just two years of its establishment, it has shaken the domestic and international security ecosystem and established itself as a 'global security powerhouse.' With a brilliant record of awards, including winning at the world's largest hacking competition, DEFCON, following sweeping victories at various domestic and international competitions, it is proving to be the 'center of South Korea's security.' <<> The whole world was amazed... The potential that echoed in Las Vegas <<> At the site of 'DEFCON 33' held in Las Vegas, USA, in August 2025. Among the over 30,000 security experts and white hat hackers gathered from around the world, the name of Soongsil University resonated the highest. The 'MMM' joint team, led by Kim Hee-chan (24th cohort), a second-year student in the Department of Information Security, won the highest honor of the competition, the 'Capture The Flag (CTF).' <<> DEFCON CTF, known as the 'Olympics of the security world,' is the most prestigious competition where the world's best hackers compete in skill. It goes beyond simply assessing technical superiority, requiring highly strategic thinking to analyze vulnerabilities in complex systems and perform real-time attacks and defenses. Kim Hee-chan formed a team with top-tier talents from South Korea, the USA, and Canada, achieving first place by a dominant margin in technical scores. <<> Professor Jo Hae-hyun, head of the Department of Information Security, stated, "Kim Hee-chan's victory goes beyond individual achievement; it is the fruit of our goal to foster 'global practical talent' and a historic event proving that our level has risen to the world's top tier. This is the result of running systematic student growth support programs, including security certifications, contests, and competitions, where they learn and practice various defense strategies applicable to real-world situations alongside theory." <<> In an interview, Kim Hee-chan also said, "The experience gained from interacting with world-class experts is an irreplaceable asset. The practical-focused education and full support provided by the department were a huge help." <<> From Year 1 to Year 2, proving fundamentals with an 'award relay' <<> The strength of Soongsil University's Information Security Department isn't just relying on one specific star player. Despite accepting its first freshmen in 2024, looking at the list of awards from 2024 to 2025 reveals remarkable 'omnidirectional activity' regardless of grade or field. <<> The 'ASCii' team, including student Lee Se-hyung (24th cohort), won the top prize in the advanced category at '2025 HackTheon Sejong,' one of the largest domestic cybersecurity competitions. Student Lee Seo-joon (24th cohort) also won an excellence award. These are achievements that gained external recognition for professional-level hacking defense capabilities beyond the university student level. Lee Se-hyung also won the grand prize at the web vulnerability competition of the '5th Honam Cyber Security Conference,' showcasing solid fundamentals even in areas aimed at revitalizing the regional security ecosystem. Lee Se-hyung said, "Web security is both the most basic and important domain in the modern IT environment. Thanks to the solid foundational education received in the department, I was able to enjoy the honor of winning." <<> The team of Kim Hee-chan and Lee Seo-joon (24th cohort) also proved their skills in power and energy sector security by winning first place at 'ELECCON 2024,' co-hosted by the Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) and a local branch of the National Intelligence Service (NIS). They also secured the grand prize at the 'Hacking Defense Competition (HACKSIUM BUSAN 2025).' <<> Even more astonishing is the skill of the 25th cohort freshmen. The team 'ps choding 3inq' (1st semester, 1st year), consisting of students Jang Hyun-soo, Kim Taek-woo, and Kim Seo-jin, caused a stir by beating seniors to take first place at 'SCON 2025.' Students Kim Seo-jin and Kim Boo-seung (25th cohort) received excellence awards at the 'Hacking Defense Competition (HACKSIUM BUSAN 2025).' Jang Hyun-soo also ranked 10th in the 16th 'SW Maestro' prompt engineering competition, proving competitiveness in next-generation technology areas where AI and security converge. <<> This is the result of Soongsil University's unique educational environment that allows students to explode their major capabilities immediately upon admission. It is not just a place that teaches hacking techniques; it is the result of segmenting the curriculum aimed at nurturing security experts with ethical awareness, architects capable of designing and protecting corporate infrastructure, and global leaders who can communicate on the world stage. Based on understanding the importance of network security, it systematically provides training in firewall configuration and intrusion detection system operation, vulnerability analysis and simulation exercises, and learning the latest security trends along with collaboration opportunities. <<> Professor Jo Hae-hyun stated, "Winning DEFCON and the successive awards in domestic competitions show the explosive potential when the potential of our students combines with the department's curriculum. We will spare no support to ensure they achieve unrivaled results in future technology fields such as AI security, quantum cryptography, and autonomous driving security." <<> A gathering place for future security leaders recognized by the nation <<> Students in Soongsil University's Information Security Department are also excelling in national-level talent development programs, not just various competitions. Students Kim Jin-ho and Ham Joo-hyuk (24th cohort) were finally accepted into the 3rd cohort of 'Whitehat School,' a next-generation security leader training program run by the Ministry of Science and ICT. Students Kwak Dong-yoon, Kim Jin-ho, Kim Hee-chan, and Choi Jung-woo (24th cohort) received the National Research Foundation of Korea Chairman's Award at the SecureX Challenge. <<> Professor Jo Hae-hyun explained, "These achievements are thanks to a 'learning community' culture where students voluntarily organize study groups and actively share knowledge between seniors and juniors. As seen in creative team names like 'Growth Cheat Anything' and 'ASCii,' students embrace security studies as an enjoyable challenge and drive each other's growth." <<> Indeed, leveraging its nature as an employment-linked contract department based on a strategic industry-academic partnership with LG Uplus, Soongsil University's Information Security Department offers the nation's first level of integrated communication and service information security education, a theory-practice integrated education covering all areas of information security, and a future-oriented specialized curriculum encompassing 5G/6G, cloud, AI, and smart network security. Furthermore, it operates project and capstone-focused practical education with direct participation from LG Uplus working-level staff, provides various internship and joint research participation opportunities during enrollment, and runs a state-of-the-art practice-centered education system reflecting actual communication infrastructure environments. <<> Strategic partnership with LG Uplus, the key to success <<> The biggest feature of the Department of Information Security, which accepted its first freshmen in 2024, is that it is an 'employment-linked contract department' specialized in the cybersecurity field, established in collaboration with LG Uplus. This short yet intense success story of Soongsil's Information Security Department was made possible with the strong backing of LG Uplus. Twenty freshmen are selected each year; they receive tuition and living expense support, and upon graduation, they are given the opportunity to join LG Uplus. <<> As hardware, software, the internet, and artificial intelligence (AI) develop, technology to securely protect the information distributed through them becomes inevitably more important. In other words, information security is a technology that will survive as long as information exists in the IT field. Students have opportunities to fulfill their dreams not only at LG Uplus but also in all IT fields, including government-funded research institutes, large corporations, and the financial sector. <<> Professor Jo Hae-hyun stated, "Beyond simple employment linkage, we support systematic student growth programs for security certifications, contests, and competition preparation. The core of our department's curriculum is that the educational process itself is a theory-practice integration covering all areas of information security, tailored to the actual needs of companies. We will lead the way in nurturing next-generation security leaders who will steer the domestic and international information security industry, based on a corporate-tailored advanced talent development model that responds to the rapidly changing security industry." <<> Exceptional benefits are also a driving force for gathering talent. Full scholarships provided to all students create an environment where students can focus solely on their studies and competition preparation without financial burden. Furthermore, providing state-of-the-art security equipment and laboratory spaces, and supporting participation in overseas conferences, serve as the foundation that turns students' dreams of becoming 'global security experts' into reality. Consequently, in this year's college admissions, Soongsil University's Information Security Department showed explosive interest and popularity (?) with competition ratios (11.58 for early decision, 8.75 for regular decision). <<> The future of South Korea's cyber defense begins at Soongsil <<> Despite its short history, Soongsil University's Department of Information Security has proven its value through skill. From Kim Hee-chan, who conquered DEFCON, the world's top competition, to the 25th cohort freshmen who lifted the championship trophy right after entering. The passion and achievements they display suggest that the future of South Korea's security industry is bright. <<> For students dreaming of becoming 'global security experts,' Soongsil University's Department of Information Security is the best choice. Heroes named 'white hat hackers' burn the midnight oil on Soongsil's campus, battling with code. The model of Soongsil University's Information Security Department, where companies and universities join hands to create the best environment and students unleash their infinite capabilities within it, is now becoming the 'standard' for security education in South Korea. The gaze of the entire nation is fixed on where those who swept the world stage will head next, and what kind of safe digital world they will create. <<> Reporter Kim Mi-young kimmy@hani.co.kr (인터넷과 정보통신의 발달과 맞물려 ‘사이버 보안’에 경고등이 켜졌다. 지난해에만 해킹의 공격으로 SK텔레콤, KT, 롯데카드, YES24, 넷마블, 쿠팡, 서울시 공공자전거 따릉이 이용자 수천 만명의 개인정보가 유출된 것이 대표적이다. 국내 주요 기업들을 겨냥한 대규모 해킹 사고가 연이어 발생하면서 IT 강국 대한민국의 보안 인프라에 심각한 우려가 제기되고 있다. 문제는 인터넷이나 와이파이, 블루투스 모듈 등 외부 네트워킹을 이용한 해킹의 위험이 단순히 개인정보 유출 피해에 그치지 않는다는 데 있다. 유출 정보는 다크웹(Dark Web)에서 거래되며 보이스피싱·스미싱·대포폰·대포통장·불법 스팸 문자 등 2·3차 범죄로 확산할 수 있다.)

item.title: Comfort and Encouragement for Slow Children and Their Parents (느린 아이와 그 부모에게 건네는 위로와 격려)
item.description:
Koh Kwang-yoon | Professor of English Language and Literature, Yonsei University
·Director of the Slow Miracle English Picture Book Museum (고광윤 | 연세대 영어영문학과 교수
·슬로우 미러클 영어 그림책 박물관 대표)

Do you have a slow child at home? I mean a child who is late to speak, slow to act, slow to learn, and practically lags behind in almost every way. Does watching such a child make you worry and feel impatient? ( 혹시 집에 느린 아이가 있나요? 말도 늦고 행동도 느리고 배우는 것도 느린, 사실상 거의 모든 면에서 뒤처지는 아이 말입니다. 그런 아이를 보며 걱정이 되고 조급한 마음이 드시나요?)

Leo, the baby tiger, can't do anything right. He can't read, can't write, and can't draw. He spills food everywhere when he eats. He can't even speak at all. His father's heart aches and feels frustrated watching Leo. But luckily, Leo had a mother who knew something. She was a mother who knew what was important for her child and knew how to put it into practice. What exactly did Leo's mother know? (아기 호랑이 레오는 제대로 할 줄 아는 것이 하나도 없습니다. 읽을 줄도, 쓸 줄도 모르고 그림도 그리지 못합니다. 먹을 때는 여기저기 흘리기만 하고요. 심지어는 말도 전혀 하지 못합니다. 그런 레오를 바라보는 아빠의 마음은 안타깝고 답답하기만 했습니다. 그런데 레오는 운 좋게도 뭔가를 아는 엄마가 있었습니다. 아이를 위해 중요한 것이 무엇인지 알고 실천할 줄도 아는 엄마였지요. 레오의 엄마는 대체 무엇을 알고 있었던 것일까요?)

This is a book for slow children, children perceived as slow, children rushed to go faster, and the parents of such children. Every parent raising a child will nod along. It will tug at your heartstrings and bring tears to your eyes. You will receive comfort and encouragement, and you will also gain conviction. (느린 아이, 느리다고 생각되는 아이, 빨리 가라고 재촉받는 아이, 그리고 그런 아이의 부모를 위한 책입니다. 아이를 키우는 부모라면 누구나 고개를 끄덕이게 됩니다. 가슴이 찡해지고 눈시울이 뜨거워집니다. 위로와 격려를 얻고, 확신도 갖게 될 것입니다.)

You can learn the aesthetics of slowness and patience. When you let go of impatience, ease and peace come. Then, even in the midst of problems, you begin to see things to be grateful for. If you know how to be grateful, you are already blessed. And a child with such parents is truly lucky. (느림과 느긋함의 미학을 배울 수 있습니다. 조급한 마음을 내려놓으면 여유와 평안이 찾아옵니다. 그러면 문제 속에서도 감사할 것이 보이기 시작합니다. 감사할 줄 안다면 당신은 이미 복 받은 사람입니다. 그런 엄마 아빠를 둔 아이는 정말 운이 좋은 것이고요.)

I hope you come to realize that there is no problem at all with being slower or less skilled than others. And that in many cases, waiting is the best and only way. I also hope children come to realize that they are good enough just as they are right now. And that it's okay to go slowly at their own pace. (알게 되길 바랍니다. 남보다 느리고 잘하지 못해도 전혀 문제가 없음을. 그리고 많은 경우 기다림이 최선이자 유일한 방법임을. 아이들도 깨닫게 되길 바랍니다. 현재 있는 모습 그대로 충분히 좋다는 것을. 그리고 자기 속도에 맞춰 천천히 가면 된다는 것을.)

Not every child grows at the same speed. There are fast children, and there are slow children. A slow child simply needs more time. Perhaps you may have to wait a bit longer. But if you keep going steadily without giving up, they will eventually succeed. (모든 아이가 같은 속도로 성장하는 것은 아닙니다. 빠른 아이가 있는가 하면, 느린 아이도 있기 마련이지요. 느린 아이는 단지 더 많은 시간이 필요할 뿐입니다. 어쩌면 조금 오래 기다려야 할지도 모르지요. 하지만 포기하지 않고 꾸준히 가다 보면 결국엔 해내게 될 겁니다.)

Why do we always want our children to be fast, and worry if they are even a little slow? A parent's faith and impatience are both passed on to the child. Please trust your child and wait for them. Help them not to give up. Support them consistently and cheer them on to the end. (우리는 왜 항상 아이가 빠르길 바라며, 조금만 늦어도 걱정할까요? 부모의 믿음도, 조급함도 아이에게 그대로 전해집니다. 아이를 믿고 기다려 주세요. 포기하지 않도록 도와주세요. 변함없이 지지하고 끝까지 응원해 주세요.)

To truly succeed at anything, you must go slowly and get each thing right one by one. That is ultimately the way to go the farthest and the fastest. It's okay to be slow, and it's okay to be late. The more that is the case, the slower and more properly you must go. (무엇이든 진짜로 성공하려면, 천천히 가면서 하나씩 제대로 해야 합니다. 그것이 결국 가장 멀리, 가장 빨리 가는 길입니다. 느려도 괜찮고, 늦었어도 괜찮습니다. 그럴수록 오히려 더 천천히, 제대로 가야 합니다.)

Do you know that slowness can be a talent, and a slow child can be even happier? A slow child is never a lacking or insufficient child. They are simply a child specialized in going slowly. So, they are a child with an advantage in practicing 'slow and steady.' As long as parents don't rush them, they can go forward steadfastly and consistently. Whether the child can grow up that way depends almost entirely on the mom and dad. (아십니까, 느림도 재능이 될 수 있고, 느린 아이가 오히려 더 행복할 수 있다는 것을? 느린 아이는 결코 모자라거나 부족한 아이가 아닙니다. 단지 느리게 가는 데 특화된 아이일 뿐입니다. 그래서 ‘천천히 제대로’를 실천하기에 유리한 아이이지요. 부모가 재촉하지만 않으면, 우직하게 꾸준히 갈 수 있는 아이입니다. 아이가 그렇게 자랄 수 있느냐는 거의 전적으로 엄마 아빠에게 달려있습니다.)

Suddenly, these words come to mind. (문득 이런 말이 떠오릅니다.)

"I am a slow walker, but I never walk backward." (“나는 천천히 가는 사람입니다. 하지만 결코 뒤로 가지는 않습니다.”)

What kind of child is your child? What kind of parent are you? (여러분의 자녀는 어떤 아이입니까? 여러분은 어떤 부모인가요?)

]]>

item.title: Preventing New Semester Syndrome Through Group Activities (모둠활동으로 신학기 증후군 예방하자)
item.description:
Kim Hyun-soo | Clinical Professor, Department of Psychiatry, Myongji Hospital
·Principal of ‘Star’ Growth School

The 2026 new semester is beginning. In the new semester, everything—grade level, friends, schedules, teachers, and classrooms—feels unfamiliar. These days, children find the new semester more difficult than before. This has even given rise to terms like ‘new semester syndrome.’ Parents and teachers need to understand that the tension and burden children feel as they start a new semester are different from the past. Only then can they understand and help the children. For today’s children, moving up a grade or transferring schools is not merely about advancing a grade or changing schools; the claim that it alters the course of their lives is not just posturing but a truth. <<> There are three main reasons why children feel greater pressure than before regarding the unfamiliarity and awkwardness of the new semester and the effort required for social adaptation. First, the most significant factor is the lack of social experience and insufficient intellectual interaction during the three years of the COVID-19 pandemic. Filling this gap is not as easy as it seems. Second, it’s due to the lack of language skills, social skills, and life skills resulting from excessive use of smartphones and social media. Third, nowadays, children often spend their vacations staying only with their parents rather than interacting and socializing with friends, extended family, and the community. Except for time at private academies, most return to group life after being alone, without experiences that foster a sense of belonging or social skills. The customs and norms of spending time with extended family members—such as relatives and neighbors—and the community have also disappeared. <<> As a result, children are sensitive about class assignments and homeroom teachers, and they feel anxious about various changes, including the location of their classroom. Among these, the biggest anxiety is the fear of not being welcomed by friends in the new class and of not naturally blending into the group of friends. When this fear grows, it can lead to physical symptoms like headaches and stomachaches, compulsive behaviors, or an increase in tardiness and absences. Some children find it uncomfortable even to breathe in the classroom and fear the onset of extreme anxiety, such as panic attacks. <<> Is there a way to resolve new semester syndrome? Here are a few suggestions. First, the parents’ attitude is crucial. They should provide reassuring confidence rather than vague worries, offer congratulations for the new school year, and make statements that convey trust. Second, it greatly helps children adapt quickly if teachers identify them individually and build good relationships. Third, various welcoming activities and those that enhance a sense of classroom belonging are also beneficial. Trying activities where children belong to a group—such as study groups, departmental activities, or clubs—would be good. This will make them happier and boost their self-esteem. Fourth, both parents and teachers should take children’s friendship issues seriously and emphasize kindness, understanding, concession, and consideration. Children most want advice on how to make a good impression on their peers. Fifth, support for school life should not be limited solely to academics, and children do not always convey all messages in words. Careful observation by parents and teachers of overall school life, an open attitude and attentive listening, and collaborative early intervention based on respect are important. <<> As attachment researcher Daniel Stern said, the beginning of the semester is a time of continuous adjustment until attunement is achieved, and how well mutual adjustment is handled is key. I hope everyone adapts well to the new semester amidst warm kindness and hope. ( 김현수 | 명지병원 정신건강의학과 임상교수
·성장학교 ‘별’ 교장

 2026년 새로운 학기가 시작된다. 새 학기에는 학년, 친구, 시간표, 선생님, 교실 등 모든 것을 낯설게 맞이한다. 요즘 아이들은 이전보다 새로운 학기를 힘들어한다. 그래서 ‘신학기 증후군’ 같은 용어도 생겨났다. 부모님과 선생님들은 새로운 학기를 시작하는 아이들의 긴장과 부담이 예전과 다르다는 것을 이해할 필요가 있다. 그래야 아이들을 이해하고 도울 수 있다. 요즘 아이들에게 진급과 전학은 단지 학년이 올라가고, 학교가 바뀌는 것이 아니라 인생의 운명을 바꾸는 일이라는 주장은 단지 허세가 아니라 진실이기도 하다.)
